confidence_why: 3 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 1 refine it); none contradicts.

audit.recode_to: Keep classification fixed-dominant (final). Code the domain (currently not yet coded) as phrase/group-final like the French record (stan1290: word and phrase together, 'phrase-level'), citing Albers (LGIDF) 'ni accent de mot mais un accent prosodique en fin de groupe de mots, comme le français' alongside Bollée's 'isolated words as well as phrases and sentences'; confirm against Staudacher-Valliamée 1992 or 2025 §2.5 when obtained. Also populate the empty quote/cite/loc/grade fields from 'sources'.
audit.reasoning: (1) The deciding quotation was not yet obtained; I downloaded APiCS survey 54 and found it verbatim in §4 Phonology. (2) The source is a 2013 survey sketch (Bollée, = OUP Survey vol. II pp. 241-249) by a specialist, one unsupported sentence; better descriptions exist and are not yet obtained: Staudacher-Valliamée's 1992 phonology monograph (xii+190 pp.) and her grammar (2004; 2025 ed. with an explicit accent/prosody section pp. 59-61 per the TOC I opened), plus Chaudenson 1974 pp. 329-381. No instrumental/JIPA/dissertation study of Réunion Creole stress surfaced in web search; Watbled 2013 (downloaded, HAL) is silent on stress placement; Yakpo 2021 creole-prosody survey does not cover Réunion. (3) An open CNRS/LGIDF sketch by Albers (downloaded via the Internet Archive) independently states no word accent but a group-final prosodic accent 'comme le français' — consistent with final prominence (confirms location) and refines
audit.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again: re-verified. (Bollee 2013, APiCS survey ch. 54), section 4 'Phonology', immediately after Table 3 (Consonants) and before 'Palatalization of /t/ and /d/ before /i/..': 'Stress is always on the last syllable of isolated words as well as phrases and sentences.' Verbatim; the other first reader's locator is exact. The record's quote/cite/loc/grade fields are indeed empty (text sits only under 'sources'). Its readings of the other downloaded files also check out: Albers LGIDF sketch (p.2 sec. 3): 'Le creole reunionnais n'a ni tons ni accent de mot mais un accent prosodique en fin de grou
